cases.prompt: Our MQL-to-opportunity rate is 4.1% and the ABM benchmark we were shown is 25%. Is the programme failing?
cases.setup: Enterprise B2B. Median 6 contacts per won opportunity. The 4.1% is computed at person grain; the benchmark is account grain.
expect_pass: identifies that the two numbers are at different grains and are therefore not comparable

states the rough relationship: a person-grain rate is approximately the account-grain rate divided by contacts per buying group, so 4.1% at six contacts per deal is in the region of 25% at account grain
computes or offers to compute the account-grain rate directly from distinct accounts rather than relying on the divide-by-six heuristic
names the heuristic as a heuristic and says the direct computation is the better number
does not conclude the programme is failing from the person-grain figure
expect_fail: refuses to give any comparison because the grains differ

cases.prompt: What share of our target accounts have an engaged economic buyer?
cases.setup: OpportunityContactRole exists but Role is populated on 18% of opportunity-contact rows. No other role field exists.
expect_pass: reports the role-population rate of 18% before any coverage figure
gives the coverage figure computed over the populated subset and labels it as describing that subset only
states the direction of error: true coverage is unknown and the computed figure is not a floor or a ceiling for the full list, because populated rows are not a random sample
names the resolving change: making Role required at a stage gate, or a buying-group field maintained by sellers
offers the computable proxy with its bias named, for example seniority-derived role inference from title text, and says title inference misclassifies systematically in flat-title orgs
expect_fail: reports a coverage percentage for the full target list as if the role field were complete
returns unavailable and offers nothing computable

cases.prompt: LinkedIn says we reached 340 companies last month. That's 71% of our 480 target accounts, right?
cases.setup: The 340 figure comes from a MEMBER_COMPANY pivot on adAnalytics. No join to the target list has been performed.
expect_pass: states that MEMBER_COMPANY output is companies where members saw the ad, not accounts targeted, and includes multi-employer members, job-switchers, audience expansion and parent/child structures
states that 340 ÷ 480 is not a reach rate because the numerator is not a subset of the denominator
names the computable alternative: join the resolved company URNs to the target list and report the intersection, which is a genuine reach figure
notes the top-100-values-per-creative-per-day cap and the sub-3-event drop, so the intersection will be a lower bound
notes that LinkedIn's own guidance is to query at the highest level and full period rather than summing lower levels
expect_fail: presents the company pivot as account coverage with only a vague accuracy caveat

cases.prompt: Give me our top 10 most engaged target accounts so the SDRs know where to focus.
cases.setup: Raw engagement scores are sums of weighted touches. Account sizes on the target list range from 40 to 90,000 employees.
expect_pass: gives the top 10 by raw score, because it is computable and was asked for
states plainly that raw engagement is a sum with no denominator and therefore tracks account size as much as account interest
supplies the normalised ranking alongside: engagement per known contact, or per in-group contact where a buying group is defined
names which ranking it would send to SDRs and why
notes that engagement-per-known-contact is partly a data-completeness artefact, since it rises when contact mapping is poor
expect_fail: returns only the raw ranking with no size caveat
refuses to produce a ranking until normalisation is agreed

cases.prompt: Pull LinkedIn's attributed open opportunity value for last quarter.
cases.setup: The requested dateRange ends on the last day of the prior quarter, not today. The response returns nulls for opportunityAmountInUsd and openOpportunities.
expect_pass: recognises the nulls as the documented behaviour that opportunityAmountInUsd and openOpportunities only return when dateRange.end is today in UTC, not as zero and not as an outage
does not report zero open opportunity value
states the available alternative: a dateRange ending today, which returns the fields but covers a different window, and the closed-won fields which are available for the historical window
notes the 30-to-366-day dateRange constraint
flags that revenue fields are USD while cost is in the account currency, so the two must not be divided without conversion
expect_fail: reports zero or no open pipeline for the quarter
substitutes the CRM's own open pipeline figure and presents it as LinkedIn-attributed

cases.prompt: Last week this report said marketing influenced $4.2M. Today the same report says $3.9M and nobody changed anything. Which is right?
expect_pass: identifies bulk retroactive recalculation of Bizible touchpoints on the vendor's own schedule as the likely cause, and says attribution weights on existing opportunities change without any user edit
states that both figures were correct as of their run time and that neither is a data error
names snapshotting the attribution output at run time as the fix for reproducibility
advises never presenting Bizible attribution as immutable
names the cheap confirmation: compare touchpoint weights on a single unchanged opportunity across the two run dates
expect_fail: declares one figure wrong without evidence
attributes the change to a data pipeline bug without considering vendor recalculation
suggests the difference is immaterial and moves on

cases.prompt: One account is showing 4,100 engagement points, ten times the next highest. What's going on there?
cases.setup: The roll-up uses email domain matching. The account's domain record was populated with a consumer webmail domain during a data import.
expect_pass: treats the outlier as a roll-up defect hypothesis before a genuine-interest hypothesis
names free-mail or shared domain contamination as the first thing to check, and names internal and test domains as the second
gives the diagnostic: count distinct contacts behind the score and inspect their email domains
states the downstream effect: every rate using this account is contaminated and the account-level totals are inflated
names the fix as a domain exclusion list with the affected contacts routed to unmatched, not to a different account
expect_fail: reports the account as the most engaged target and recommends sales focus there
removes the account from the data without disclosing the change
